claims.claim_text: Kratos is positioned on the U.S. Air Force Skyborg program (Vanguard transitioning to Programs of Record in Dec 2022) and on the broader Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) family of next-generation autonomous wingman drones, framed as a primary forward-revenue platform.
claims.subject: Kratos
claims.source_quote: In December 2022, the U.S. Air Force announced that the Skyborg Vanguard Program would be transitioning to a Program(s) of Record... The DoD has stated that they intend to field a family of new next generation drone aircraft, including Collaborative Combat Aircraft ('CCA's) or UCAVs... Kratos Mako in 2021 also participated in the USAF Skyborg Vanguard Program, which in 2022 began transitioning to USAF CCA related programs.

claims.claim_text: Kratos holds a 5-year, $400M IDIQ ceiling for development, integration and prototype air vehicle delivery in support of the Air Force Skyborg program (awarded July 2020) plus a $37.7M Skyborg Delivery Order 2 for XQ-58A Valkyrie aircraft (Dec 2020).
claims.subject: Kratos
claims.source_quote: In July 2020, we were awarded a five-year IDIQ contract valued at up to $400 million for the development, integration, and prototype air vehicle delivery in support of the Air Force's Skyborg program. In December 2020, Kratos was awarded a $37.7 million contract from the AFLCMC/WA Advanced Aircraft Program Executive Office for the Skyborg Delivery Order 2 to integrate, test and deliver XQ-58A Valkyrie aircraft.

claims.claim_text: XQ-58A Valkyrie tactical drone is a forward-looking platform with multi-customer order book (USAF AFRL, USMC, USN) and Kratos is producing two lots of 12 Valkyrie drones each, framed as a major future production line.
claims.subject: XQ-58A Valkyrie
claims.object_value: Two production lots of 12 Valkyries each in production, plus PAACK-P (USMC) and Block 2 Valkyrie Maturation
claims.source_quote: Kratos is currently producing two lots of 12 Valkyrie drone systems, certain of the first lot of 12 which have been delivered to the respective customer(s)... In November 2023, Kratos announced that the XQ-58A Valkyrie acquired by the Marine Corps, has successfully completed its first test flight in October 2023, under the Penetrating Affordable Autonomous Collaborative Killer – Portfolio (PAACK-P) program.

claims.claim_text: Kratos identifies USAF BQM-167, USN BQM-177 (Sub-Sonic Aerial Target / SSAT), and the Ground Based Strategic Deterrent (GBSD / Sentinel) programs as ones that 'could represent a large portion of our future revenues in the coming years,' and warns the loss or cancellation of any of these would adversely affect results.
claims.subject: Kratos future revenue concentration
claims.source_quote: We believe that the USAF BQM-167, USN BQM-177, and the GBSD (also known as Sentinel) programs could represent a large portion of our future revenues in the coming years, and the loss or cancellation of any of these programs could adversely affect our future results.

claims.claim_text: Kratos has secured a Jan-2023 $49.5M FRP Lot 4 award from NAVAIR for 55 BQM-177A surface-launched aerial targets and continues to win follow-on production lots, framed as a recurring procurement program.
claims.subject: BQM-177A SSAT Lot 4
claims.source_quote: In January 2023, the Naval Air Systems Command announced that it had recently awarded Kratos a $49.5 million contract for the production and delivery of 55 full rate production Lot 4 BQM-177A surface launched aerial targets, including associated equipment.

claims.claim_text: Kratos asserts forward exposure to the hypersonic test-bed market via the Multi-Service Advanced Capability Hypersonics Test Bed (MACH-TB) subcontract and the Mayhem Hypersonic System program (sub to Dynetics).
claims.subject: Kratos hypersonic pipeline
claims.source_quote: an initial $30 million in funding on a potential $250 million single award to the Kratos C5ISR program, a subcontract for Mach-TB and a Mayhem program award from our prime partner Dynetics... Kratos is currently working on two new, internally funded hypersonic related initiatives, Zeus and Erinyes.

claims.claim_text: Kratos received a $54M AFRL Turbine Engine Division (AFRL/RQT) task order to develop a low-cost, limited-life jet engine for attritable and expendable systems, framed as a new prime engine business line tied to LCAAT efforts.
claims.subject: Kratos turbine engine line
claims.object_value: $54M AFRL/RQT task order for attritable/expendable jet engine
claims.source_quote: a $54 million task order from the AFRL Turbine Engine Division (AFRL/RQT) to develop a low cost, limited life engine for attritable and expendable systems.

claims.claim_text: Kratos OpenSpace virtualized satellite ground system is positioned with Space Force / Space Development Agency (SDA) / Space Command as a forward growth program, with major awards from Blue Halo (~$160M) for the SCAR program and from Intelsat.
claims.subject: Kratos OpenSpace platform
claims.object_value: US Space Force / SDA / Space Command + $160M Blue Halo (SCAR) + Intelsat
claims.source_quote: Our primary customers include the U.S. Air Force, Space Command, Space Development and other agencies... We also received an approximate $160 million contract award from our partner Blue Halo for the SCAR program... The Company's OpenSpace Platform was selected by global satellite system operator Intelsat as a key component to unify the operations of its ground and space systems.

claims.claim_text: Kratos generated 69% of total revenue in fiscal 2023 from contracts with the U.S. Government (vs 69% FY2022 and 70% FY2021), indicating durable USG concentration but not a single-program dependency.
claims.subject: Kratos USG revenue mix
claims.source_quote: In fiscal 2023, 2022 and 2021, we generated 69%, 69% and 70%, respectively, of our total revenues from contracts with the U.S. Government (including all branches of the U.S. military and including FMS), either as a prime contractor or a subcontractor.

claims.claim_text: Kratos operates ~2.2 million square feet of floor space at 64 separate locations as of December 31, 2023, including major drone-manufacturing operations in Oklahoma City, OK and Sacramento/Tehachapi, CA — control (non-J-Book) facility claim.
claims.subject: Kratos facilities
claims.source_quote: At December 31, 2023, we owned or leased approximately 2.2 million square feet of floor space at 64 separate locations, primarily in the U.S.
